items.title: In the Strait of Hormuz, Iran has unleashed a plot against the West that was years in the making
items.description: By moving so much of the war into the Strait of Hormuz and Persian Gulf, Tehran has hit its adversaries where it hurts the most. Analysts warn that while the United States military is mighty, history shows in asymmetrical warfare, the lesser power can win the day.

items.title: Live: 'Will not be safe': Iran threatens global tourist sites as US sends more Marines
items.description: Iran's military threatens to hunt down US and Israeli officials and army commanders even while they are on holiday or visiting entertainment centres. Follow live.

items.title: What experts say is likely to happen to Australia's fuel supply from mid-April
items.description: The government is responding to fuel shortages due to the war in the Middle East and says Australia has enough supply until mid-April. Here's what experts say could happen after that.

items.title: Live: NT communities in for 'a rough 24 hours' as TC Narelle 'rapidly' approaches
items.description: The category two system is expected to strengthen today as it heads towards the Northern Territory. Follow live.

items.title: The election where second place matters most
items.description: Both polls and pundits are expecting Labor to comfortably win today's SA election, but exactly who Labor will be beating — and who it will face in the next parliament — is the key question.

items.title: Long waits, frustration as technical glitches delay voting in SA
items.description: Voters complain to the ABC about long queues and trouble being signed off the electoral roll at polling places across the state.

items.title: Buffy The Vampire Slayer star Nicholas Brendon dies at 54
items.description: Nicholas Brendon, best known for his role as Xander Harris in all seven seasons of Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died aged 54.

items.title: Federal politics is about to become all about the gas industry
items.description: Scott Morrison's assertion that the chase to secure vaccines in early 2021 was "not a race" cost him dearly. A similar global contest is already underway, only this time it involves securing energy supplies.

items.title: These kids beat cancer, but treatments caused long-term health issues
items.description: Maya and Angus both survived childhood cancer, but the treatments that saved their lives left them with chronic health issues. Experts say better care is needed for childhood cancer survivors.

items.title: How Matildas defender Kaitlyn Torpey's 'goldfish mentality' is taking her to new heights
items.description: A Ted Lasso lesson, and an Australian indie rock classic, are inspiring Kaitlyn Torpey to take her career to new heights, as she prepares for tonight's Women's Asian Cup final.

items.title: Live: Star Tiger out with a hamstring against Suns, as Tassie makes VFL history
items.description: Richmond is reunited with the man who led them to three premierships in the last decade as Gold Coast looks to maintain its perfect start to the year. Follow live.

items.title: Live: New-look Knights face Warriors without its two biggest stars
items.description: The Newcastle Knights are without their two biggest names as they host the New Zealand Warriors in a clash of two unbeaten teams. Follow live.

items.title: Perth teen charged with alleged indecent assault of 14 women at exercise spots
items.description: Police charge a teenager after he allegedly assaulted 14 women while they were exercising in Perth's northern suburbs.

items.title: Your teenage son might learn something from Married at First Sight
items.description: Watching the largely fake, but also completely true, juggernaut reality TV series Married at First Sight with our 14-year-old was never a deliberate choice but it is potentially very powerful.

items.title: 50/50 quiz: 2000s hip-hop, planets in retrograde and disturbing TV puppets
items.description: Every question has only two options: one is right and the other is wrong. You have an even chance of guessing correctly each time.

items.title: Finding an escape from modern life in the booming world of arts and crafts
items.description: Craft trends come and go, but a resurgence in social arts and crafts is proving that creativity and human connection are still very much in vogue.

items.title: Why Ryan Gosling's eyes were so important to Project Hail Mary
items.description: With most of Project Hail Mary's action taking place in far off corners of space it was up to Australian cinematographer Greig Fraser to create what we've never seen.

items.title: Donor devastated as charity plans to sell land despite agreement not to
items.description: A charity known for the landmark separation of conjoined twins Krishna and Trishna lists a regional Victorian property for sale against the wishes of its donor.

items.title: Earth's low orbit is becoming cluttered with high-velocity space junk
items.description: Thousands of satellites are being launched into space at low Earth orbit, joining hundreds of thousands of pieces of space junk, and it's becoming a real problem.

items.title: Thousands told to evacuate as Hawaii officials warn 120yo dam could fail
items.description: Thousands of residents in Hawaii have been warned to evacuate towns north of Honolulu as floodwaters inundate streets and damage homes.

items.title: Chuck Norris, film star and martial artist, dies aged 86
items.description: Norris's epic fight with kung fu superstar Bruce Lee in The Way of The Dragon helped him become an icon, and he went on to star in more than 20 movies.

items.title: The anonymous letters police say could help solve a 35-year mystery
items.description: Mark Gregory was killed in a 1991 hit-and-run collision. Now, police believe a series of anonymous letters could hold the key to unlocking the 35-year mystery.

items.title: Dramatic footage shows moment flames engulf Melbourne ice-cream shop
items.description: Two teenage boys have been arrested after the store in Tarneit, in the city's west, was destroyed by fire early this morning.

items.title: Why Australia's first major aviation disaster remained a mystery for 27 years
items.description: When eight people vanished without a trace in 1931, Australia's first major airline disaster became a 27-year mystery that gripped the nation, until a hiker's chance discovery changed everything.

items.title: Swapping Mandarin for Auslan has profound impact at Canberra school
items.description: Mount Rogers Primary School in Canberra is the only public school in the ACT to teach Australian Sign Language as its second language.
